rows.title: Colorado lawmakers are targeting hospital facility fees. Here’s why that’s a big deal.
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1215 would ban hospitals from charging facility fees for most outpatient visits, ending what proponents say is an unnecessary add-on that boosts hospitals’ bottom line

rows.title: Three members of Colorado’s congressional delegation seek $60 billion to reduce wildfire risk, restore Western land
rows.standfirst: The Protect the West Act is sponsored by U.S. Sens. Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper, as well as U.S. Rep. Jason Crow

rows.title: Colorado added thousands of child care slots in “day care deserts” in just two years
rows.standfirst: The legislature approved the child care expansion program in November 2020 during a special session to help the state recover from the COVID pandemic

rows.title: SNAP benefits drop at least $90 a month in Colorado as food, housing, heating and fuel prices rise
rows.standfirst: Some anticipate a 20% increase in people needing help as SNAP benefits that expanded during the pandemic return to previous levels

rows.title: COVID pushed Colorado nonprofits to their limits. Leaders stuck around, committed to the mission, not the money.
rows.standfirst: As the next wave of economic challenges lines up, top managers say they’d rather fight to help clients than jump on the corporate track

rows.title: This trio of Colorado innovators is transforming the way we camp
rows.standfirst: Flated Air-Topper, Radica MoonLander and Tune M1 offer new designs for camper toppers on trucks

rows.title: Cycling journalists form Escape Collective following layoffs, exodus from Outside
rows.standfirst: As Outside Inc. slashes budgets as investors tighten belts, Escape Collective enlists thousands of subscribers in first 24 hours

rows.title: One tiny zebra mussel was found in a Colorado reservoir. It will be 5 years before the water gets an all-clear.
rows.standfirst: Aquatic biologists began spraying to kill the invasive species at Highline Lake State Park on Wednesday. Park managers are worried decontamination procedures will kill boat traffic.

rows.title: What’s Working: How a Denver nonprofit is expanding the benefits of work
rows.standfirst: Plus: The rise in employee benefits, Fair Workweek bill dies, and more!

rows.title: Aging activists have battled for decades to clean up a Colorado Superfund site. Who will fight once they’re gone?
rows.standfirst: The Cotter Uranium Mill Superfund site has an estimated 5.8 million tons of radioactive waste buried under the dirt

rows.title: Exxon drops algae research, but Colorado labs press on in hunt for green fuel
rows.standfirst: Technologies that are quicker to scale now are ExxonMobil’s focus. The Colorado labs the petroleum giant funded still see potential in algae as a biofuel.

rows.title: More than 80% of local governments have opted out of Colorado’s new paid family, medical leave
rows.standfirst: Many said they have similar or better programs in place for their workers. The deadline to opt out is March 31.

rows.title: Colorado oil and gas companies offer $459 million to guarantee their wells are plugged eventually
rows.standfirst: The plans seek to meet new state financial requirements, but some smaller operators are hoping to put up only a fraction of the needed funds.

rows.title: The park ranger, the mental health worker and the endless hurdles they face to help people on Denver’s streets
rows.standfirst: A program pairing mental health clinicians with the rangers who field complaints about camping in parks aims to get people into therapy, if they’re willing

rows.title: What’s Working: Tipping for fast food, to-go pick ups, pot and … wedding gowns?
rows.standfirst: Coloradans share their tipping tales.Plus: One restaurant’s “No Tips” policy, Colorado Restaurant Association’s stance on tipping, and more!

rows.title: A Louisville family begins construction on a new home where the Marshall fire destroyed their last one
rows.standfirst: Louie Delaware and his family said their idea to build a new “living in place home” helps soften the blow of what they lost in the 2021 fire.

rows.title: Digging into Colorado’s top consumer complaints, from the death of robocalls to incompetent contractors
rows.standfirst: Notably absent for the second year in a row were fraudulent and unwanted telephone calls.

rows.title: Xcel Energy will cut Colorado bills again in April as natural gas costs continue to fall
rows.standfirst: While the state’s largest utility is under fire for unsustainable energy bills hitting consumers late in 2022, Xcel has also cut gas costs four times in six months.

rows.title: HOA foreclosures “lose-lose” game for Coloradans, but these lawyers win regardless of the outcome
rows.standfirst: A retired NFL player’s legal battle with a homeowners association spotlights why critics say Colorado law incentivizes attorneys to advise that HOAs foreclose on residents rather than find less expensive solutions.

rows.title: Colorado’s push to lower hospital costs has a catch: The state also needs hospitals’ money
rows.standfirst: Hospitals say House Bill 1215, which would limit their ability to charge facility fees, will ultimately impact funding for Medicaid

rows.title: Suncor will finally reopen after a 3-month closure. But will anything change for its neighbors?
rows.standfirst: Gas prices that rose when Colorado’s only petroleum refinery closed are expected to drop. But residents who’ve dealt with Suncor’s pollution for decades aren’t so thrilled — and they have a plan.

rows.title: Regulation falls short of protecting north Denver residents from Suncor refinery, nonprofit research finds
rows.standfirst: Cultivando, an Adams County environmental nonprofit advocating for Latino communities, released the results of their yearlong air monitoring program and called for stricter industry regulations

rows.title: Will Frozen Dead Guy Days stay true to its roots as it moves to the ritzy Stanley Hotel in Estes Park?
rows.standfirst: As the festival starts its new life this weekend, will Visit Estes Park’s mission to “professionalize it” improve it or ruin it?

rows.title: Coloradans can expect more than $2.5 billion in tax refunds — as long as the economy doesn’t tank
rows.standfirst: Two quarterly economic and tax revenue forecasts presented to the Colorado legislature Thursday had good and bad news

rows.title: How Colorado homeowners still reeling from the COVID pandemic can apply for financial assistance
rows.standfirst: The money will help homeowners pay their mortgages, homeowner association fees or liens, utilities, delinquent property taxes and homeowner’s insurance

rows.title: Samples from Front Range oil and gas wells detect seeping natural gas, benzene and other chemicals
rows.standfirst: Colorado regulators say the subset of wells tested were known to be troubled, and many have already been plugged and abandoned

rows.title: Colorado governor, Democrats unveil major effort to boost housing by directing local land-use policy. Here’s what it would do.
rows.standfirst: The measure would prevent Colorado’s largest cities from limiting construction of accessory-dwelling units, duplexes and triplexes and require them to let multifamily units be built near transit centers.

rows.title: Health insurers balk at price demands in Colorado governor’s signature health insurance program
rows.standfirst: In new regulatory filings, insurers say they cannot lower prices enough to meet the Colorado Option’s goals

rows.title: Vail Resorts settles with family of New Jersey man who died in Colorado chairlift accident
rows.standfirst: The children of Jason Varnish sued after his jacket became entangled on a chairlift with a raised seat and died of positional asphyxiation in 2020.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s unemployment rates weren’t what you thought they were
rows.standfirst: Revised estimates, low survey response rates and meager budgets can be blamed — or credited? — for the changes. Plus: Unemployment backlog resolved, reader tax tips and more!

rows.title: Shearing season brings workers from around the world to harvest wool from Colorado sheep
rows.standfirst: Colorado is consistently one of the Top 5 wool producing states and it takes deft hands with special training for the harvest.

rows.title: A facelift has spruced up Colorado’s Pops the Triceratops. Next comes a big reveal back at the fossil’s Weld County home.
rows.standfirst: Artists in Fruita are putting the finishing touches on the fossil’s new display. The work follows Denver Museum of Nature and Science exam that found Pops may be much older than originally thought.

rows.title: Crested Butte “buying into community values” with plan to become first Colorado municipality to go all-electric
rows.standfirst: A survey of residents to craft the town’s comprehensive plan prods Crested Butte council to adopt strict new building codes that prohibit natural gas in new buildings

rows.title: A modular home community near Telluride may become a national model. But getting it open hasn’t been easy.
rows.standfirst: Pinion Park residents are settling into Norwood. Among the lessons learned: don’t ship, assemble and finish the homes in winter.

rows.title: 81-year-old Englewood man arrested in the ax killings of his wife, daughter
rows.standfirst: Police say Reginald Maclaren told them he killed his wife and daughter because they had lost their apartment and had no other place to live.

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers’ inaction on rising property tax bills stokes another ballot measure arms race
rows.standfirst: Gov. Jared Polis and Democrats, who control the Capitol, say they are committed to coming up with a long-term fix this year. But with the 2023 legislative session more than halfway over and no public proposal, fiscal policy nonprofits are filling the vacuum.
